name: Viking Sack of Paris, Ragnar's Raid
summary: A Norse fleet of 120 ships and 5,000 warriors under a leader the Franks call "Ragnar" (possibly Ragnar Lothbrok) sails up the Seine and sacks Paris on Easter Sunday 845. Charles the Bald cannot mount an effective defense and pays a ransom of 7,000 pounds of silver (the first of many Danegeld payments) to persuade the Vikings to leave. The raid demonstrates that Carolingian defenses are inadequate against seaborne attackers.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Paris raid inaugurates a cycle of Viking tribute payments that drain Carolingian financial reserves and undermine royal prestige; the repeated failure of Carolingian kings to protect their cities accelerates the rise of local counts and bishops as effective defenders, the feudal decentralization that defines 10th-century France; the siege of Paris in 885-886 will be more dramatically resisted but at greater cost
